fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Vehicle Parking Area; Detached Structure; Open Lawn Area; Landscaped Area; Access Drive; Walkway
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Vehicle Parking Area
fr.recommendations:
• Trim vegetation along the access drive to maintain clearance for emergency vehicles approaching the main residence.
• Mark the driveway entrance with reflective address numbers visible from the road in both directions.
• Keep a clear path between the vehicle parking area and the main residence entrance so responders can reach the front door without navigating around parked vehicles.
• Thin dense vegetation near the detached structure to allow responders to reach and move around it without obstruction.
• Keep the rear access point unlocked and free of parked vehicles or stored items that would block emergency entry.
• Mark any rear or side gate latches with reflective tape so responders can locate them quickly in low visibility.
• Keep the walkway between the main residence and detached structure clear of stored items, equipment, or overgrown landscaping.
• Cut back dense vegetation along the property perimeter where it limits the ability of responders to move around the outside of the main residence.
• Designate and keep clear a flat, firm area near the access drive that emergency vehicles can use for staging without blocking the main entry or exit.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Open Terrain; Ground Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Mixed Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Route
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees in the cluster nearest to the structure to increase open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove shrubs that are growing directly against or within a few feet of the structure.
• Trim lower branches on scattered trees near the structure so branches do not hang close to the ground.
• Keep ground vegetation mowed or cut short in the area immediately surrounding the structure.
• Clear any dead or dry ground vegetation that has built up along the single access route.
• Keep the driveway and access route free of overhanging branches so emergency vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Mark the single access route clearly so it is easy to identify for emergency responders approaching the property.
• Clear vegetation and debris from the rear of the property to improve movement around the structure where access is limited.
• Separate mixed shrubs and trees growing in combined masses near the structure by thinning or removing plants to create open gaps.
• Keep the area between scattered shrubs and the structure open by removing plants that have grown into that space.
